_provenance.subject: minimum wage (economics / labour policy)
_provenance.source: Prism public API — research.evidence (one call per angle)
_provenance.note: Counts and shares measured from the data. Quoted findings verbatim and verified. Two angles fell to the subject lane (0 and 2 both-sides papers) and are reported that way, not charted as established.

angles.claim: raising the minimum wage increases consumer prices
angles.reading: the literature on this is actively contested — a large share of papers frame it as a problem, a caution or a criticism
angles.note: framing is contested, but the high-tier documents actually read converge on yes — near-full price pass-through
evidence: "we show that restaurant prices rise in response to minimum wage increases" (Aaronson, J. Human Resources 2008)
"near-full price pass-through of minimum wages" (Ashenfelter & Jurajda, McDonald's, J. Labor Econ 2022)
"nearly all of the minimum wage increase is passed through to consumers" (Allegretto & Reich 2025)

angles.claim: raising the minimum wage reduces employment
angles.reading: mostly positive framing, with a substantial cautionary minority
angles.note: the textbook claim — well studied, genuinely unsettled, lean near zero; the read document found no adverse effect
evidence: "I find no evidence that these small, incremental increases ... have an adverse effect on hours worked or the job destruction rate" (Bishop 2018)

angles.claim: raising the minimum wage reduces poverty
angles.reading: mostly positive framing, with a substantial cautionary minority
angles.note: the deepest lane, but qualifying papers (351) outnumber supporting (250) — heavily hedged, no net lean

angles.claim: raising the minimum wage reduces teenage employment
angles.lane_note: only 2 papers cover both sides; the famous NYS study finds a −20% teen-employment effect, another finds well-off teens gain at the expense of poorer ones — but the both-sides title lane is almost empty

angles.claim: raising the minimum wage causes small business closures
angles.lane_note: zero papers cover both sides of this claim (the phrase 'small business closures' appears in one title) — the alarm has essentially no direct research lane, against ~2,959 news mentions

stance_composition_pct.what: share of papers that support / qualify / contradict each claim, normalised to 100%
